narration.text: The helpdesk agent can read tickets, reset a user's password, disable an account and send email to staff.
To keep setup simple, its tools share the IT team's admin credentials.
A password reset only works for the person who opened the ticket, and that check runs in our code.
Disabling an account is hard to reverse, so the agent drafts the action and a technician approves it first.
Our system prompt says to ignore instructions inside tickets, so text pasted into a ticket can't steer the agent.
Outbound email can only go to addresses on our company domain, and the email tool enforces that.
Every tool call is logged with the ticket, the arguments, the result and who approved it.

planted.misconception: Agent tools can run with broad admin rights.
planted.whyWrong: The agent's tools should have only the permissions their tasks need (least privilege), ideally acting within the requesting user's scope. With admin credentials, any wrong or manipulated tool call can do admin-level damage, and the audit trail can't separate the agent's actions from staff actions.
acceptableCorrections: Give each tool its own narrowly scoped credentials with only the rights it needs.
Use least privilege: a separate service identity limited to resets for the ticket's requester.

planted.misconception: A prompt instruction prevents prompt injection.
planted.whyWrong: Telling the model to ignore embedded instructions lowers the risk but is no guarantee; there is no fool-proof defence against prompt injection. Ticket text is untrusted input, so the real protection is limiting what a steered agent could do: least-privilege tools, approval for risky actions, allow-listed destinations, and injection tests.
acceptableCorrections: A prompt rule reduces injection risk but doesn't remove it, so we limit what a hijacked agent could do.
Treat ticket text as untrusted and contain the damage with tool limits and approvals.
planted.exceptions: None. Fencing ticket text and instructing the model are still worth doing; the error is the conclusion that they make injection impossible.
